notes: Note 2: Unspecified routes are those where the port of load/unload has not been supplied by data providers or where the port of load/unload is an offshore installation in international waters.
Note 3: Data for roll-on/roll-off traffic for Hull in 2019 has been revised.
Note 4: Data for container (lo-lo) and roll-on/roll-off traffic for London from 2019 to 2023 has been revised.

Note 5: In 2025, freight traffic data on two new cargo type breakdowns were collected from major UK ports: wood pellets (previously categorised as ‘other dry bulk’) and wind farm products (previously categorised as ‘other general cargo’). Totals for ‘other dry bulk’ and ‘other general cargo’ will appear lower in 2025 due to this cargo recategorisation.

Note 6: Due to data system changes at a large operator at London, some cargo category 2025 figures for roll-on/roll-off (ro-ro) are not aligned with previous years. This does not affect the total figure for all ro-ro traffic, only 'Road goods vehicles with or without accompanying trailers', 'Unaccompanied road goods trailers and semi-trailers' and 'Rail wagons, shipborne port-to-port trailers and shipborne barges' which are estimated by the operator. DfT are reviewing these figures with the operator, and they will likely be revised in the next release.
method: DfT PORT0499 (major ports, port level) summed by port, year, direction, cargo group and region of the port of load (inwards). A year in which a port reported nothing to DfT's major-port statistics is null, not zero. Ports included: the 51 major ports with data in 2025. Locations: DfT's rough location where it gives one, otherwise EMODnet's main-port location for the same UN/LOCODE.
